narrative:
##SUMMARY##
Funding rates edged lower this week, hinting at modest easing. The drop in SOFR and DVP Repo Rate each by 0.01 percentage points reduces the cost of short-term borrowing. Total bank credit slipped by $25.1 billion, a sign of slight tightening in overall credit supply. Yet commercial loans grew by $46.7 billion, indicating strong demand for financing. Deposit growth at both large and small banks supports liquidity in the system. On balance, the data point to marginally looser funding conditions.

##FRESH:sofr##
SOFR was 3.89 percent on 2026-10-05. It slipped 0.01 percentage points from the prior period. The marginal decline eases short-term funding costs.

##FRESH:effr##
EFFR stood at 3.88 percent on 2026-10-05. It was unchanged from the prior reading. Stable rates suggest steady pricing for overnight funding.

##FRESH:iorb##
IORB held at 3.9 percent on 2026-10-04. There was no change from the prior period. Consistent rates keep inter-bank borrowing conditions flat.

##FRESH:bank_credit_total##
Total bank credit measured $19.86 trillion on 2026-09-23. It fell $25.1 billion from the prior period. The dip signals a modest tightening in overall credit availability.

##FRESH:commercial_loans##
Commercial loans reached $2.93 trillion on 2026-08-01. They rose $46.7 billion from the prior period. Growing loan balances point to expanding credit demand.

##FRESH:dvp_overnight_rate##
DVP Repo Rate was 3.88 percent on 2026-10-07. It declined 0.01 percentage points from the prior period. The lower repo rate marginally reduces funding costs for dealers.

##RECENT##
Tri-Party Repo Rate rose to 3.89 percent, up 0.01 percentage points. US M2 Money Supply increased to $23.34 trillion, up $124.9 billion. Treasury General Account fell to $880.3 billion, down $68.4 billion. Overnight Reverse Repo rose to $1.0 billion, up $0.2 billion. Large Bank Deposits grew to $19.64 trillion, up $66.3 billion, while Small Bank Deposits rose to $5.67 trillion, up $3.2 billion. Total Bank Assets climbed to $25.93 trillion, up $142.2 billion. GCF Repo Rate rose to 3.94 percent, up 0.03 percentage points. Foreign Official Treasury Holdings fell to $3.77 trillion, down $5.0 billion. Japan Treasury Holdings slipped to $1.1 trillion, down $12.7 billion. China Treasury Holdings declined to $618.0 billion, down $15.4 billion. UK Treasury Holdings rose to $998.3 billion, up $58.5 billion.

##WATCH##
Watch for any further moves in short-term rates such as SOFR and the DVP Repo Rate. Monitor the trajectory of total bank credit versus commercial loan growth for signs of credit tightening. Keep an eye on Treasury General Account balances as they influence market liquidity. Observe foreign official holdings for potential shifts in overseas demand for U.S. Treasuries.
